title: `c.header()` crashes after consumption of the finalized res body
Feature Request: Bearer Auth - allow custom error response content type
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

## Problem  

Bearer auth error responses can't be sent as anything other than `application/json` or `text/plain`. The content type is hardcoded in `throwHTTPException`...

## Request
 
Since we want to adhere to [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9457/) problem details (`application/problem+json`) everywhere, it would be nice if we are able to customize the content type in the response. Since the middleware throws an `HTTPException` with a pre-built `res`, an `onError` handler can't fix the headers afterwards either. See for Reference [bearer-auth/index.ts](https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/main/src/middleware/bearer-auth/index.ts#L146-L152)

## Idea

Let `MessageFunction` also return a `Response` and use it as-is (set `WWW-Authenticate` if missing). Backwards compatible. Alternatively a `contentType` option next to `message` (?)
  
Current workaround: throw from the message function and rebuild the `WWW-Authenticate` header manually in the app.

title: [Discussion] make Hono ESM only in next major version
body:
**Hono should drop CJS support in next major version and go ESM only**

right now Hono is published as a dual package with both cjs and esm support, 
but there isn't any widespread usage of hono in pure cjs context [[sourcegraph search for require("hono")](https://sourcegraph.com/search?q=context:global+require(%22hono%22)&patternType=keyword&sm=0)]

there is lot of typescript code that looks like imports but is compiled down to CJS under the hood, but I think its fine. Current supported Node releases are 22, 24, and 26. Node 20 is EOL. [`require(esm)`](https://joyeecheung.github.io/blog/2025/12/30/require-esm-in-node-js-from-experiment-to-stability/) is already supported across all supported node versions including node 20. Node is only one of Hono's target runtime where we need CJS and that issue is mostly solved, on runtimes like Bun/Deno/Cloudflare we don't have any use for CJS.

So I think we should, raise minimum supported version for hono to node >=22 and remove all tooling for CJS and publish hono@5 (next major) as a ESM only version.

Refs:
- https://antfu.me/posts/move-on-to-esm-only
- https://e18e.dev/blog/migrating-the-ecosystem-to-esm.html
- https://storybook.js.org/blog/storybook-is-going-esm-only

Open PR: https://github.com/honojs/hono/pull/5114

title: Custom LinearRouter and PatternRouter ignore strict trailing-slash routing
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.8

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

Node.js 22.23.2

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use either `LinearRouter` or `PatternRouter` with the default `strict: true` setting:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { LinearRouter } from 'hono/router/linear-router'

const app = new Hono({ router: new LinearRouter() })
app.get('/hello', (c) => c.text('ok'))

const response = await app.request('http://localhost/hello/')
console.log(response.status)
```

The same happens with `PatternRouter`. It also affects parameter routes such as `/users/:id` when the request is `/users/42/`.

### What is the expected behavior?

With strict routing enabled by default, a route should only match the same trailing-slash form. `/hello` should not match `/hello/`, and `/hello/` should not match `/hello`.

`RegExpRouter` and `TrieRouter` already return 404 for those cases.

### What do you see instead?

`LinearRouter` returns 200 for `/hello` matched against `/hello/` and for `/users/:id` matched against `/users/42/`.

`PatternRouter` returns 200 for both directions, including `/hello/` matched against `/hello`.

### Additional information

The difference comes from `LinearRouter` accepting one trailing slash in its exact-route checks and `PatternRouter` adding an optional trailing slash to ordinary route patterns. This makes the public `strict` option depend on the selected router.

title: JSX: Allow non-array JSXNode function components
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

Hello,
I would love to be able to create function components using the `jsx` function, like below:

```js
export function Partial({ name, children, tag = "div", ...rest }) {
  return jsx(tag, { "x-partial": name, ...rest }, children);
}
```

However, this will give me a Typescript error:
```
'Partial' cannot be used as a JSX component.
  Its type '({ name, children, tag, ...rest }: PartialProps) => JSXNode' is not a valid JSX element type.
    Type '({ name, children, tag, ...rest }: PartialProps) => JSXNode' is not assignable to type '(props: never) => FunctionComponentResult'.
      Type 'JSXNode' is not assignable to type 'FunctionComponentResult'.
        Type 'JSXNode' is not assignable to type 'HtmlEscapedString'.
          Type 'JSXNode' is not assignable to type 'string'.
```

A workaround I now use is wrapping the jsx call in an array:
```js
return [jsx(tag, { "x-partial": name, ...rest }, children)];
```
This will work fine, but I would see a method returing a single JSXNode work too.
Is there any reason its now working this way?

Also, I didn't find the `jsx` method documented. I think there are good use cases for it, for writing "real" JSX isn't always my favorite option. Preact does document it for their similar functionality: https://preactjs.com/guide/v10/api-reference/#h--createelement

aws-lambda: a binary `+xml` response is corrupted (`application/vnd.apple.installer+xml`)
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.13.8 (`main`, `098e1191`)

### What runtime/platform/OS are you using?

`bun` 1.4.3 on macOS — the `aws-lambda` adapter, so this happens for anyone serving files from AWS Lambda (API Gateway, Function URLs or ALB).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Return a file whose `Content-Type` ends in `+xml`, from an app running on AWS Lambda.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { handle } from 'hono/aws-lambda'

const app = new Hono()

app.get('/app.pkg', (c) =>
  c.body(pkgBytes, 200, { 'content-type': 'application/vnd.apple.installer+xml' })
)

export const handler = handle(app)
```

`application/vnd.apple.installer+xml` is the media type of an Apple installer package. That file is **not XML** — it is a `xar` archive, so the first bytes are `xar!` (`78 61 72 21`) followed by binary integers and a compressed stream.

The same happens with any media type that ends in `+xml` but holds a binary archive, for example `application/vnd.mozilla.xul+xml`.

### What is the expected behavior?

The response body should be byte-for-byte identical to what the app returned. The adapter should treat this content type as binary and send it base64 encoded.

### What do you see instead?

The body gets decoded as UTF-8, so every byte that is not valid UTF-8 turns into U+FFFD and the file is corrupted. There is no error and nothing is logged — the download just silently comes out broken.

I traced it with a debugger. `defaultIsContentTypeBinary()` dec

title: LinearRouter matches an empty path segment and returns an empty param
body:
`LinearRouter` matches a path with an empty segment and hands the handler an empty param. The other three routers return 404.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { LinearRouter } from 'hono/router/linear-router'

const app = new Hono({ router: new LinearRouter() })
app.get('/u/:id/posts', (c) => c.json({ id: c.req.param('id') }))

await app.request('http://localhost/u/42/posts')  // 200 { id: "42" }
await app.request('http://localhost/u//posts')    // 200 { id: "" }   <- expected 404
```

| Router | `/u//posts` |
| --- | --- |
| RegExpRouter | 404 |
| TrieRouter | 404 |
| PatternRouter | 404 |
| LinearRouter | 200, `id` is `""` |

A handler that expects an id to be present gets an empty string instead.

### Cause

In `match()`, the plain label branch already rejects an empty segment at the end of the path but not one in the middle:

```ts
let endValuePos = path.indexOf('/', pos + 1)
if (endValuePos === -1) {
  if (pos + 1 === path.length) {
    continue ROUTES_LOOP      // trailing empty segment, rejected
  }
  endValuePos = path.length
}
value = path.slice(pos + 1, endValuePos)
```

For `/u//posts` the `indexOf` returns `pos + 1`, so `value` is `''` and the match carries on. That is why `/a/:p` correctly 404s on `/a/` but `/u/:id/posts` matches `/u//posts`.

Fix is to reject `endValuePos === pos + 1` the same way. Full suite passes and I added the case to `common.case.test.ts`, where all four routers pass it. Happy to open the PR.

title: accepts() matches media types and language tags case-sensitively
body:
`accepts()` compares the accept header entry and the supported value as raw strings, so a client that varies the case gets the default instead of a match.

```ts
const app = new Hono()
app.get('/', (c) =>
  c.text(accepts(c, { header: 'Accept', supports: ['text/html'], default: 'application/json' }))
)

// Accept: text/html  -> text/html
// Accept: TEXT/HTML  -> application/json
```

| Header | Value | supports | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accept | `text/html` | `['text/html']` | `text/html` |
| Accept | `TEXT/HTML` | `['text/html']` | default |
| Accept | `Text/Html` | `['text/html']` | default |
| Accept-Language | `en-US` | `['en-US']` | `en-US` |
| Accept-Language | `en-us` | `['en-US']` | default |
| Accept-Language | `EN` | `['en']` | default |

Both are case-insensitive. Media types by RFC 9110 §8.3.1, language tags by RFC 4647 §2.1. `en-us` is the one I would expect in the wild, since the uppercase region subtag is only a convention.

### Cause

```ts
// src/helper/accepts/accepts.ts
const matchType = (acceptType: string, supportedType: string): boolean => {
  if (acceptType === supportedType) {
    return true
  }
  ...
  return acceptMain === supportedMain
}
```

Nothing case-folds. The subtype wildcard path has the same problem, so `TEXT/*` does not match `text/html` either.

This is the same bug #5060 reported for `Content-Type`. #5064 fixed it for `parseBody()` and `validator()`, but `accepts()` was not part of that change.

PR is up. `defaultMatch()` r

jsx/dom: improve keyed children reconciliation for large list updates
body:
## What is the feature you are proposing? I would like to improve the reconciliation performance of large keyed child lists in `hono/jsx/dom`. The current reconciliation logic searches the existing children array with `findIndex()` and removes matched children with `splice()`. This is not an issue for small lists, but it can scale poorly when large tables or log viewers handle selection, filtering, sorting, or reordering. ## Use case For example, a parent component may manage both table rows and selection state: ```tsx const [rows, setRows] = useState(initialRows) const [selectedIds, setSelectedIds] = useState([]) return ( <> {rows.map((row) => ( ))}
) ``` Changing only the selection state causes the parent component to run again, so `rows.map()` creates the keyed children again. Reordering also changes the DOM order in real applications: ```tsx setRows((rows) => [...rows].reverse()) ``` These patterns occur in data tables, log viewers, file lists, chat histories, and drag-and-drop interfaces. ## Current behavior In a local Bun benchmark with 5,000 keyed elements, the current implementation produced: - approximately 12.5 million array movements even when the order did not change - approximately 12.5 million key comparisons when reversing the list - app

title: Refactor: Replace unused map() with forEach() in Hono.on() route registration
Widen Context<any>'s untyped get/set fallback to accept symbol keys
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

`Context<E>`'s untyped fallback (when `E` is `any`, i.e. plain `new Hono()` / `Context` with no `Variables` generic) resolves `get`/`set` to a `Record<string, any>`-keyed shape:

```ts
// context.d.ts
set: Set<IsAny<E> extends true ? {
    Variables: ContextVariableMap & Record<string, any>
    ...
```

`Record<string, any>`'s key type only covers `string | number`, so calling `c.set`/`c.get` with a `symbol` key fails to compile — the same `Argument of type 'unique symbol' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'` shape as #2484, but for `symbol` instead of a plain string.

The runtime has no such restriction: `set`/`get` store into a `Map` internally, which accepts a `symbol` key without any issue. This is purely a type-level gap, not a real limitation.

**Motivating case:** small frameworks building on top of Hono (mine included — a thin DI/routing layer) often want to stash an internal per-request marker on the context using a `Symbol()` key specifically *because* it can't collide with any string key a user of the framework might set. Today that requires an `as never` cast to work around the type, even though nothing at runtime objects.

**Proposed change:** widen the `IsAny<E>` fallback so it also accepts `symbol` keys, e.g.:

```ts
Variables: ContextVariableMap & Record<string, any> & { [key: symbol]: any }
```

This only changes the *untyped* `Context<any>` branch — anyone using `Hono<{ Variables: {...} }>()` with a con

Suffix wildcard routes (/foo*) return 404 when a sub-app has static + :param routes with the same method
body:
## Version

hono 4.12.29 and 4.13.1 (latest)

## Expected behavior

A suffix wildcard route like `/assets*` should match `/assets/app.js` regardless of what else is registered on the app.

## Actual behavior

When a mounted sub-app registers a static route and a `:param` route as siblings (same method), every suffix wildcard route (`/assets*`) on the parent app silently returns 404. Slash-star (`/assets/*`) is unaffected.

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'

// control: works without the sub-app
const control = new Hono()
control.get('/assets*', (c) => c.text('ok'))
console.log((await control.request('http://x/assets/app.js')).status) // 200

// bug: same wildcard, but sub-app has static + :param siblings
const app = new Hono()
const sub = new Hono()
sub.post('/items', (c) => c.text('items'))
sub.post('/:slug', (c) => c.text('slug'))
app.route('/api', sub)
app.get('/assets*', (c) => c.text('ok'))
console.log((await app.request('http://x/assets/app.js')).status) // 404
```

## What I tried

- Removing either `/items` or `/:slug` makes it work again
- Different methods (`get('/items')` + `post('/:slug')`) is fine
- `{slug}` instead of `:slug` also fixes it
- Confirmed on 4.12.29 and 4.13.1

## Related issues

#4975, #4623 — same router-fallback family, but those cover `/**` with param-vs-param conflicts; this is suffix-`*` with a static-vs-param conflict.

title: ETag middleware should not generate ETag on 4xx or 5xx
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

Current ETag middleware always generates `ETag` and returns 304 if `If-None-Match` matches, regardless of the response status.
If a route returns the same response body (like `{}`) for different statuses, and the client cached the response and ETag, the client cannot distinguish between the response statuses.

So I want ETag middleware to generate etag only for 200 response,
and to maintain backward compatibility, I propose adding `cacheableStatusCode: number[] | undefined` option like cache middleware.
(The default would be all status codes)

title: StreamingApi.pipe(): WritableStream writer lock permanently lost when pipeTo() throws
body:
## Summary

`StreamingApi.pipe()` releases the `WritableStreamDefaultWriter` lock before calling `pipeTo()`, but only re-acquires a new writer on the success path. If `pipeTo()` rejects — for example when the client disconnects, the upstream `ReadableStream` errors, or an abort signal fires — the `getWriter()` call on line 81 is never reached. `this.writer` is left pointing to the already-released (stale) writer, and `this.writable` has no active writer attached to it.

Any subsequent call to `write()`, `writeln()`, or `close()` on the same `StreamingApi` instance then hits one of two failure modes:

* `TypeError: This WritableStream writer has been released and cannot be used to monitor the stream's state.` (from the stale writer), or
* `TypeError: Failed to execute 'getWriter' on 'WritableStream': The stream is locked to a writer.` if `pipeTo()` left the stream in a locked-but-abandoned state.

Both outcomes silently break the stream for the caller. The error handlers registered with `onAbort()` or the outer `stream()` wrapper do not restore the writer, so post-pipe writes are dead with no diagnostic.

## Affected Code

`src/utils/stream.ts`, lines 78-82 (v4.12.23, present since pipe was introduced):

```ts
async pipe(body: ReadableStream) {
  this.writer.releaseLock()                            // lock released here
  await body.pipeTo(this.writable, { preventClose: true })  // throws → jumps out
  this.writer = this.writable.getWriter()             // never reached on thr

title: Proposal: add overloads to `useRef` type to match React's API
body:
## Context

When using `hono/jsx` hooks to write code that mirrors React-style patterns, `useRef` returns a ref whose `.current` is always typed as `T | null`, even when initialized with a non-null value.

```ts
const ref = useRef(new Map<string, number>())
ref.current.set('a', 1) // ❌ TS error: 'ref.current' is possibly 'null'.
```

This is because `useRef` currently has a single signature:

```ts
// hono/src/jsx/hooks/index.ts
export declare const useRef: <T>(initialValue: T | null) => RefObject<T>
// where RefObject<T> = { current: T | null }
```

The runtime implementation always returns `{ current: initialValue }`, so when a non-null initial value is passed, `.current` cannot actually be `null` at first read. The nullable type is purely a TypeScript-level limitation.

## React behavior (for comparison)

React provides overloads so that `useRef(value)` returns a non-nullable ref, while `useRef<T>(null)` keeps the nullable shape needed for DOM refs:

```ts
function useRef<T>(initialValue: T): MutableRefObject<T>
function useRef<T>(initialValue: T | null): RefObject<T>
function useRef<T = undefined>(): MutableRefObject<T | undefined>
```

## Proposal

Add matching overloads to `hono/jsx`'s `useRef` so that users get non-nullable `.current` when they pass a non-null initial value. Implementation does not need to change — this is a type-only fix.

I'm happy to submit a PR if this direction is welcome. Wanted to check first whether the single-overload signature was intentional

title: `useSyncExternalStore` doesn't resubscribe when `subscribe` function changes
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.12.31

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

chrome 150.0.7871.181

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Clone repo https://github.com/pajecawav/hono-usesyncexternalstore-subscribe-repro
2. `pnpm install && pnpm dev` and open http://localhost:4173/
3. Click "Increment" 
4. Click "Reset"

title: etag middleware ignores `If-None-Match: *` wildcard (RFC 9110 §13.1.2)
body:
## Problem
`etag` middleware's `etagMatches` never treats `If-None-Match: *` as a match, so a `*` wildcard request never yields `304 Not Modified` when a representation exists (RFC 9110 §13.1.2).

## Cite
`src/middleware/etag/index.ts:32-36`
```ts
function etagMatches(etag: string, ifNoneMatch: string | null) {
  return (
    ifNoneMatch != null && ifNoneMatch.split(/,\s*/).some((t) => stripWeak(t) === stripWeak(etag))
  )
}
```
`stripWeak('*') === stripWeak('"abc"')` is `'*' === '"abc"'` = false.

## Steps
1. `app.use(etag()); app.get('/', c => c.text('hi'))`
2. `curl -H 'If-None-Match: *' http://localhost/`

## Expected
`304 Not Modified` (representation exists).

## Actual
`200 OK` with body.

## Env
hono `4.12.27`, TypeScript `^5.9.2`.

No test in `src/middleware/etag/index.test.ts` covers the `*` case.

Thanks for maintaining honojs/hono!

title: TrieRouter: /* wildcard does not match empty remainder after a regexp-constrained param
body:
### Description
In TrieRouter, a `/*` wildcard registered after a regexp-constrained param — e.g. `/:id{[0-9]+}/*` — does not match the empty remainder (bare path `/12`), even though the plain-param form `/:id/*` does. Non-empty remainders (`/12/y`) match; only the empty-remainder case is broken.

### Steps to reproduce
```ts
import { TrieRouter } from 'hono/router/trie-router';
const router = new TrieRouter();
router.add('GET', '/:x{[0-9]+}/*', 'W');
router.match('GET', '/12'); // observed: 'W' not matched; expected: 'W' matches
```
Matrix:
```
/:x/*          @ /12   → matches   (correct)
/:x{[0-9]+}/*  @ /12   → no match  (BUG — expected: matches)
/:x{[0-9]+}/*  @ /12/y → matches   (correct)
/:x{[0-9]+}/*  @ /abc  → no match  (correct)
```

### Root cause
`src/router/trie-router/node.ts` `search()`: the RegExp-match branch pushes `child`'s handlers but never collects `child.#children['*']` for the empty remainder, unlike the plain-param branch which does (`if (isLast) { … if (child.#children['*']) pushHandlerSets(…) }`). The two branches are asymmetric.

### Suggested fix
In the RegExp branch, when the match consumes the whole remaining path (`m[0].length === restPathString.length`), also push `child.#children['*']` handler sets — mirroring the plain-param branch and keeping the RegExp branch's own argument order. This fixes the empty-remainder case with no effect on non-empty remainders, the plain-param path, or non-matching inputs; the router test suite passes.

_Distinct

title: RPC headers not merging when function
aws-lambda handler misinterprets V1 events as V2 events when using base path mappings
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.12.8

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

AWS API Gateway V1

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. deploy hono app as AWS lambda function
2. integrate the lambda as REST API in the API Gateway
3. add a base path mapping for a custom domain in the API Gateway
4. invoke the API via the custom domain

### What is the expected behavior?

hono interprets the lambda event as an `APIGatewayProxyEvent`, using the `path` property as path for the route, thereby correctly stripping the base path from the base path mapping.

### What do you see instead?

hono sees a `rawPath` property, even though it's deployed as a REST API, thereby interpreting the lambda event as `APIGatewayProxyEventV2` and mistakenly using the `rawPath` as path for the route.

### Additional information

Though barely documented, when adding a base path mapping in AWS API Gateway, AWS adds a `rawPath` property to the APIGatewayProxyEvent for REST APIs, containing the original path before the base path mapping was applied.

This confuses hono into thinking it's an APIGatewayProxyEventV2, even though the app was integrated into a REST API (API Gateway V1) and not into a HTTP API (API Gateway V2), thereby using the wrong path for the routes (and potentially also misinterpreting other properties).

title: serveStatic treats empty string content as not found
body:
## Summary

`serveStatic` allows `getContent()` to return `Data | Response | null`, and `Data` includes `string`. However, the middleware uses a truthiness check to decide whether content was found. A valid empty string body (`''`) is therefore treated as not found and falls through to `onNotFound` / `next()`.

## Code path

Type / adapter / consumer anchors:

- `src/context.ts:26`: `Data` includes `string`.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:37`: `getContent` may return `Data | Response | null`; `null` is the explicit absence sentinel.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:86`: the middleware consumes the adapter/custom `getContent()` result.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:88-89`: `Response` gets a separate found branch.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:92`: non-`Response` data is classified by `if (content)`.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:119`: found data is returned with `c.body(content)`.
- `src/middleware/serve-static/index.ts:122-123`: falsy data falls into `onNotFound` and `next()`.

## Steps to reproduce

Validation level: dynamic branch probe plus source-control-flow validation.

```ts
baseServeStatic({
  getContent: async () => '',
})
```

For a request that reaches this `getContent`, `''` is a valid `Data` value but follows the not-found branch because it is falsy.

Local branch probe:

```text
"" -> not-found-next-branch
"non-empty" -> found-branch
new Uint8Array(0) -> found-branch
new ArrayBuffer(0) -> found-branch
new Response(""

title: Proposal to change to specifying `charset` parameter individually for each MIME type
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

Currently, MIME types parameter are set through mechanical determination.

https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/fa8eef707990e80a593fa32c2f67713a2ecd2e9b/src/utils/mime.ts#L16-L18

title: compress() middleware should change etags to weak
body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.12.9

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

n/a

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```
import {compress} from 'hono/compress';

const app = new Hono()
  .use(compress())
  .get('/', async(c) => {
    c.header('ETag', '"strong-etag"');
    return c.text('<response long enough to trigger gzip compression>')
  });
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The `compress` middleware is compressing a response which has an assigned `ETag`. Since it modifies the original response, it's no longer byte-to-byte equivalent. It's a functional equivalent.

For such cases, the response should switch to a __weak__ `ETag` instead.

In the example above, this header:
```
ETag: "strong-etag"
```
should be automatically changed into:
```
ETag: W/"strong-etag"
```

Otherwise it breaks range requests, since the response is no longer a byte-to-byte equivalent.

### What do you see instead?

The `compress` middleware incorrectly leaves the custom `ETag` as is, despite modifying the response.

### Additional information

_No response_

title: Since PR #4393, success response types can no longer be resolved without explicit status/ok checks
body:
PR https://github.com/honojs/hono/pull/4393 improved the ability to get accurate types for specific status codes. While this is a great improvement on its own, it is causing an issue in my project.

In my project, we centrally manage 4xx and 5xx errors using a customized fetch function. Our design allows individual UI components to handle only the success cases. Previously, this meant our UI components were type-safe without needing to explicitly check the response code.

However, since v4.10.0 (where https://github.com/honojs/hono/pull/4393 was released), we can no longer resolve the types without checking status or ok in each UI component. As a result, we are forced to add these checks to every single API call site. This negatively affects the codebase by reducing readability (due to increased boilerplate) and increasing the bundle size.

Is there a way to maintain type safety without manually checking status or code, just as we were able to do before? Any advice would be appreciated.

_Originally posted by @baseballyama in https://github.com/honojs/hono/discussions/4575_

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Calling `parseBody()` followed by `text()` or `json()` on the same request throws `TypeError: bodyCache[anyCachedKey].then is not a function`.

This happens when `Content-Type` is **not** `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (e.g., `application/json` or no Content-Type header).

**Root cause:**
`parseBody()` stores a resolved plain object in `bodyCache.parsedBody` (via `??= await parseBody(...)`). When Content-Type is not a form type, `parseBody()` returns `{}` immediately without going through `formData()`, so `parsedBody` is the only key in `bodyCache`.

`#cachedBody()` then picks it up via `Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]` and calls `.then()` on it, assuming every cache entry is a `Promise`.

When Content-Type **is** a form type, `parseBody()` internally calls `request.formData()` which goes through `#cachedBody('formData')`, caching a `Promise` under `bodyCache.formData` first — so `Object.keys()[0]` is `'formData'` and `.then()` succeeds.

**Reproduction:**

```typescript
import { HonoRequest } from 'hono/request'

const req = new HonoRequest(
  new Request('http://localhost', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ event: 'push' }),
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  })
)
await req.parseBody()  // returns {}, cach

title: link rel=canonical is silently removed when it shares the same href as link rel=alternate hreflang
body:
First of all, thank you for building Hono — it's been a joy to work with, especially the JSX renderer's automatic head hoisting. I ran into a small edge case while implementing hreflang + canonical links, and I'd love to help get it fixed.

## Bug Report

### Summary

When using `jsxRenderer`, a `<link rel="canonical">` tag is silently dropped from the rendered HTML if a `<link rel="alternate" hreflang="...">` tag shares the same `href`.

### Reproduction

On a localized EN page (e.g. `/en/about`), the canonical URL and the `hreflang="en"` alternate URL are identical by design. When both are declared in the renderer:

```tsx
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/en/about" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/about" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="ja" href="https://example.com/ja/about" />
```

The rendered HTML becomes:

```html
<!-- canonical is missing -->
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/about" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="ja" href="https://example.com/ja/about" />
```

### Root Cause

In `src/jsx/intrinsic-element/common.ts`, the deduplication key for `link` elements is:

```ts
const deDupeKeyMap = {
  link: ["href"],
}
```

The deduplication logic in `src/jsx/intrinsic-element/components.ts` uses **OR semantics**: if *any* key in `deDupeKeys` matches an existing tag's props, the new tag is considered a duplicate.
